cards.title: Bias in Free-Concentration Scaling for PTA
cards.claim: In the low-extraction binding scenarios studied in SUP013, back-calculating free exposure distributions from total concentrations with an average fu can misrepresent the free-exposure variance and bias extreme-quantile PTA/cutoff estimates; incorrectly adding fu variability can increase that bias. This is not a universal prohibition on modeling binding or a guaranteed bias direction for every drug.
conditions: Applies when PK/PD index is based on free drug (e.g., fAUC/MIC, fT>MIC).
Relevant when total concentration data is scaled by fu.
Bias magnitude depends on the true distribution of fu and the target PTA level.
limitations: In SUP013's specified binding/low-extraction simulations, scalar-fu back-calculation from total exposure misrepresented free-exposure variance and extreme-quantile PTA. Test applicability before transferring this limitation.
Incorrectly adding fu variability in the source's back-calculation scenarios increased bias; preserve any justified covariance instead of assuming independent binding draws.
cards.downstream_use: Method qualification for PTA simulations; correction of historical PTA analyses.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
